items.markdown:
In Hebrew grammar, the definite article is the prefix letter **ה** (pronounced *ha-*), which attaches to the front of a noun to mean "the".[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iu9VXGSs7_U)[[2]](https://www.hebrewpod101.com/blog/2021/03/18/hebrew-grammar-overview/)

### The Definite Article (ה)

- **How it works:** It attaches directly to the start of a word (e.g., *suse* meaning "horse" becomes *ha-suse* meaning "the horse").[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j6nSs9IMmOA&t=16)
- **No indefinite article:** Hebrew does not have an indefinite article like "a" or "an" in English . A plain noun like *suse* can mean "a horse" depending on the context.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZSYJ4JESMvc&t=10)[[2]](https://www.hebrewpod101.com/blog/2021/03/18/hebrew-grammar-overview/)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iu9VXGSs7_U)
- **No gender distinction:** Unlike some languages, the same prefix **ה** is used for masculine, feminine, singular, and plural nouns.[[1]](https://www.hebrewpod101.com/blog/2021/03/18/hebrew-grammar-overview/)
- **Guttural changes:** When attached to words starting with guttural letters (like **א**, **ה**, **ח**, **ע** , or **ר** ), the vowel under the *hey* often changes from a short pathah to a long vowel like *qamets* or *segol* because gutturals reject a doubling dagesh.[[1]](https://hebrew4christians.com/Grammar/Unit_Four/The_Definite_Article/the_definite_article.html)[[2]](https://uhg.readthedocs.io/en/latest/particle_definite_article.html)
- **Proper nouns:** Names of people and specific cities are already considered definite, so they do not take the article.[[1]](https://hebrew4christians.com/Grammar/Unit_Four/The_Definite_Article/the_definite_article.html)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j6nSs9IMmOA&t=16)

### Newspaper or Website Articles
If you meant "article" in the journalistic or literary sense (like a piece in a newspaper), Hebrew uses two main terms according to [Ulpan La-Inyan](https://ulpan.com/how-to-say-article-in-hebrew/):

- **כְּתָבָה (*ketavah*):** An informational article that presents facts so the reader can form their own conclusion.
- **מַאֲמָר (*ma'amar*):** An opinion or essay-style article where the author shares their own perspective.[[1]](https://ulpan.com/how-to-say-article-in-hebrew/)
